exercises.en: My older sister is reading an encyclopedia in her room.
exercises.why: Action verb stem + 고 있다 means "is ___ing".

exercises.en: My friend is cutting the map with scissors.
exercises.why: 고 attaches straight to the stem 자르, with no change.

exercises.ko: 어젯밤 열한 시에 저는 교과서를 읽고 ___.
exercises.en: At eleven last night I was reading the textbook.
exercises.why: Put 있다 in the past (있었어요) to say "was ___ing".

exercises.en: Minsu knows my major.
exercises.why: 알고 있다 is the common way to say you know something.

exercises.en: A soldier is standing over there.
exercises.why: For the state of standing, use 서 있다, not 서고 있다.

exercises.en: My younger sibling is lying on the bed.
exercises.why: 눕다 is ㅂ irregular, and the lying state uses 누워 있다.

exercises.en: The weather is getting cold these days.
exercises.why: An adjective needs 아/어지다 before 고 있다: 춥다 becomes 추워지고.

exercises.en: My skin got much better.
exercises.why: 좋다 + 아지다 gives 좋아지다, past 좋아졌어요.

exercises.en: I am living in Seoul with my parents.
Do you have a calculator?
My shoulder is getting better.
My friend is sitting in front of the desk.

reading.ko: 지금은 새벽이에요. 저는 책상 앞에 앉아 있어요. 저는 대학생이에요. 제 전공은 영어예요. 지금 교과서를 읽고 있어요. 비가 오고 있어요. 날씨가 추워지고 있어요. 제 동생은 침대에 누워 있어요.
reading.en: It is dawn now. I am sitting in front of my desk. I am a university student. My major is English. I am reading a textbook now. It is raining. The weather is getting cold. My younger sibling is lying on the bed.

questions.q: What time of day is it?
What is the writer's major?
What is the younger sibling doing?

exercises.ko: 이 방이 저 방___ 더 넓어요.
exercises.en: This room is more spacious than that room.
exercises.why: 보다 goes on the thing you compare against: "than".

exercises.ko: 제 언니는 라면___ 밥을 더 좋아해요.
exercises.en: My older sister likes rice more than ramen.
exercises.why: 라면 is what rice is compared against, so it takes 보다.

exercises.en: This ramen is less spicy than that ramen.
exercises.why: 덜 means "less".

exercises.en: Minsu is the tallest on our team.
exercises.why: 제일 (or 가장) makes a superlative: "the most".

exercises.en: I like winter more than summer.
exercises.why: With 보다, 더 says "more"; 가장/제일 don't combine with 보다.

exercises.en: This department store is the biggest in Seoul.
exercises.why: The group you pick the most from is marked with 에서.

exercises.en: My younger sibling is lazier than me.
exercises.why: 게으르다 is 르 irregular (게을러요); 보다 alone already shows "more".

exercises.en: Today I got up earlier than usual.
exercises.why: 평소보다 means "than usual".

exercises.en: My older brother's salary is more than mine.
This chair is the most comfortable.
This road is narrower than that road.
I want to talk more with my friend.

reading.ko: 저는 한식을 아주 좋아해요. 양식보다 한식을 더 좋아해요. 저는 매운 음식을 제일 좋아해요. 제 친구 민수는 한식보다 양식을 더 좋아해요. 민수는 매운 음식을 저보다 덜 좋아해요. 우리는 오늘 시내에서 같이 점심을 먹을 거예요.
reading.en: I like Korean food a lot. I like Korean food more than Western food. I like spicy food the most. My friend Minsu likes Western food more than Korean food. Minsu likes spicy food less than I do. Today we will have lunch together downtown.

questions.q: What food does the writer like the most?
Which does Minsu prefer, Korean or Western food?
Where will they eat lunch today?

exercises.en: Minsu is very good at cooking.
exercises.why: The skill takes 을/를 with 잘하다, and 요리 ends in a vowel.

exercises.en: I can't go on the business trip tomorrow.
exercises.why: 못 before a verb means "can't"; 안 would mean "won't".

exercises.en: I couldn't translate that novel.
exercises.why: Stem + 지 못하다 means "couldn't".

exercises.en: I can't chew this meat.
exercises.why: Stem + 지 못하다: 씹다 becomes 씹지 못해요.

exercises.en: That is my fault.
exercises.why: 잘못 written as one word is the noun "fault, mistake".

exercises.en: I opened the wrong door.
exercises.why: As one word, 잘못 means "wrongly, by mistake".

exercises.en: I can't read Korean well.
exercises.why: With a space, 잘 못 means "can't do well".

exercises.en: Did you sleep well last night?
exercises.why: 잘 is the adverb "well" and goes right before the verb.

exercises.en: My older sister (said by a man) is good at English.
I can't eat meat.
I couldn't go to school yesterday.
That was my mistake.

reading.ko: 제 친구 민수는 수영을 아주 잘해요. 하지만 요리는 못해요. 어제 민수가 라면을 만들었어요. 그 라면은 너무 매웠어요. 저는 매운 음식을 못 먹어요. 저는 그 라면을 먹지 못했어요.
reading.en: My friend Minsu is very good at swimming. But he is bad at cooking. Yesterday Minsu made ramen. The ramen was too spicy. I can't eat spicy food. I couldn't eat that ramen.

questions.q: What is Minsu good at?
What was wrong with the ramen?
Why couldn't the writer eat it?
questions.a: The writer can't eat spicy food.

exercises.en: When did you graduate from university? (formal)
exercises.why: Past stem 했 ends in a consonant, so it takes 습니까.

exercises.en: Is this road narrow? (formal)
exercises.why: 좁 ends in a consonant, so the formal question is 습니까.

exercises.en: Do you know that person? (casual, to a child)
exercises.why: A ㄹ stem drops ㄹ before 니: 알다 becomes 아니.

exercises.en: Is this room too small? (soft question)
exercises.why: An adjective with a consonant stem takes 은가요.

exercises.en: Is that person a professor? (soft question)
exercises.why: With a noun, use 이다 + ㄴ가요: 교수인가요.

exercises.en: Did your friend already go home? (soft question)
exercises.why: With verbs, the soft question ending is 나요, also after 았/었.

exercises.en: Who won yesterday?
exercises.why: 누구 + 가 contracts to 누가.

exercises.en: Where is Minsu now?
exercises.why: To ask where a person is, use 어디에 있어요.

exercises.en: Why did you take a nap?
When do you leave the hospital?
Who did you meet at the wedding?
Do you like comic books? (casual, to a child)

reading.ko: 제 친구 민수는 지난주에 입원했어요. 오늘 저는 병원에 갔어요. 저는 민수에게 만화책을 주었어요. 민수는 만화책을 아주 좋아해요. 민수는 병원에서 낮잠을 많이 자요. 민수는 다음 주에 퇴원해요.
reading.en: My friend Minsu went into the hospital last week. Today I went to the hospital. I gave Minsu a comic book. Minsu really likes comic books. Minsu takes a lot of naps in the hospital. Minsu leaves the hospital next week.

questions.q: When did Minsu go into the hospital?
What did the writer give Minsu?
When will Minsu leave the hospital?

exercises.en: How do I attach this file?
exercises.why: 어떻게 asks "how, in what way" and goes before the verb.

exercises.en: How is this lotion?
exercises.why: 어때요 asks for an opinion: "How is it?"

exercises.en: What novel did you read?
exercises.why: Before a noun, use 무슨, not 뭐 or 무엇.

exercises.en: What did you eat yesterday?
exercises.why: "What" is the object here, so 뭐를 = 뭘.

exercises.ko: 이 두 치마 중에서 ___ 치마가 더 예뻐요?
exercises.en: Of these two skirts, which skirt is prettier?
exercises.why: 어느 picks one from a known set.

exercises.en: How many eggs did you eat?
exercises.why: 몇 + counter asks "how many".

exercises.en: How long does it take to get to school?
exercises.why: 얼마나 asks about amount or degree, like "how long".

exercises.en: What is the most delicious at this restaurant?
exercises.why: A question word as subject takes 이/가, never 은/는.

exercises.en: How was the movie?
What kind of book do you like?
How many days were you in Seoul?
How many people came?

reading.ko: 지난주에 저는 부산에 다녀왔어요. 부산까지 버스로 네 시간쯤 걸렸어요. 부산의 바다는 아주 예뻤어요. 저는 시장에서 생선을 먹었어요. 생선이 아주 맛있었어요. 다음에 다시 가고 싶어요.
reading.en: Last week I went to Busan and came back. It took about four hours to Busan by bus. Busan's sea was very pretty. I ate fish at the market. The fish was very delicious. I want to go again next time.

questions.q: Where did the writer go last week?
How long did the bus take?
What did the writer eat at the market?

exercises.en: The sky is very blue.
exercises.why: 파랗다 is ㅎ irregular: ㅎ drops and the vowel becomes ㅐ.

exercises.en: My friend's car is white.
exercises.why: 하얗다 drops ㅎ and becomes 하얘요.

exercises.en: I like red apples.
exercises.why: Before a noun, ㅎ simply drops: 빨갛다 becomes 빨간.

exercises.en: This flower is yellow.
exercises.why: 노랗다 drops ㅎ and becomes 노래요.

exercises.en: Is winter in Korea always like this?
exercises.why: 이렇다 is ㅎ irregular: 이래요.

exercises.en: Yes, that's right. I'm a student.
exercises.why: 그래요 is the usual reply for "that's right".

exercises.en: I want to buy a shirt like that one over there.
exercises.why: Before a noun, 저렇다 becomes 저런.

exercises.en: You wash this bowl like this.
exercises.why: Before a verb, use the adverb 이렇게 "in this way".

exercises.en: My bag is purple.
I bought a black skirt.
I want to buy a pink shirt.
Why is your face so red?

reading.ko: 오늘 아침에 눈이 많이 왔어요. 길이 아주 하얘요. 저는 회색 셔츠와 갈색 치마를 입었어요. 제 친구는 분홍색 셔츠를 입었어요. 우리는 같이 학교에 걸어갔어요. 하늘은 회색이었어요. 저는 이런 날씨를 좋아해요.
reading.en: It snowed a lot this morning. The road is very white. I wore a grey shirt and a brown skirt. My friend wore a pink shirt. We walked to school together. The sky was grey. I like weather like this.

questions.q: What happened this morning?
What color was the writer's skirt?
What color was the friend's shirt?

exercises.en: I came to Korea two years ago.
exercises.why: Time amount + 전에 means "ago".

exercises.en: I drink water before taking a bath.
exercises.why: Verb stem + 기 전에 means "before doing".

exercises.en: I drink milk before going to sleep.
exercises.why: Verb stem + 기 전에; 자다 becomes 자기 전에.

exercises.en: After the movie ended, we ate dinner.
exercises.why: "After doing" uses ㄴ/은 후에, not 기.

exercises.en: After eating lunch, I drank coffee.
exercises.why: 먹 ends in a consonant, so it takes 은 before 후에.

exercises.en: Class starts in thirty minutes.
exercises.why: Time amount + 후에 means "later, from now".

exercises.en: I will arrive at the police station within ten minutes.
exercises.why: Time amount + 안에 means "within".

exercises.en: Since I started exercising, I have become healthier.
exercises.why: 이래로 follows the ㄴ/은 form, like 후에.

exercises.en: I met my friend three days ago.
exercises.ko: 저는 삼 일 전에 친구를 만났어요.

exercises.en: I exercise before going to work.
I will go to Busan in two days.
exercises.ko: 저는 이틀 후에 부산에 갈 거예요.

exercises.en: After watching the movie, I went home.

reading.ko: 저는 일 년 전에 한국에 왔어요. 한국에 온 이래로 매일 한국어를 공부하고 있어요. 저는 학교에 가기 전에 운동해요. 수업이 끝난 후에 친구들과 시내를 구경해요. 집에 온 후에 숙제를 해요. 저는 자기 전에 한국 영화를 봐요.
reading.en: I came to Korea a year ago. Since coming to Korea, I have been studying Korean every day. I exercise before going to school. After class ends, I look around downtown with friends. After coming home, I do homework. Before going to sleep, I watch a Korean movie.

questions.q: When did the writer come to Korea?
What does the writer do before school?
What does the writer do before going to sleep?

exercises.en: Everyone knows that rumor.
exercises.why: 모든 goes directly before a noun: "every".

exercises.en: Someone took my wallet.
exercises.why: 누군가 means "someone" (unknown person).

exercises.en: Nobody came yesterday.
exercises.why: 아무도 + a negative verb means "nobody".

exercises.en: On the holiday I didn't go anywhere.
exercises.why: 아무 데도 + negative means "nowhere".

exercises.en: Anything is fine with me.
exercises.why: 아무거나 means "anything at all"; 아무것도 needs a negative verb.

exercises.en: I drink coffee every morning.
exercises.why: Noun + 마다 means "every, each".

exercises.en: I want to travel to Southeast Asia someday.
exercises.why: 언젠가 means "someday"; 언제나 means "always".

exercises.en: That park is always quiet.
exercises.why: 언제나 means "always, every time".

exercises.en: There is something in my bag.
I didn't eat anything today.
Every student is reading a textbook.
I go for a walk every morning.

reading.ko: 저는 기숙사에 살고 있어요. 기숙사의 모든 방에 책상이 있어요. 저는 아침마다 기숙사 앞에서 산책해요. 지난 휴일에는 기숙사에 아무도 없었어요. 모두 고향에 갔어요. 저는 아무 데도 안 갔어요. 언젠가 저도 고향에 가고 싶어요.
reading.en: I live in a dorm. Every room in the dorm has a desk. Every morning I take a walk in front of the dorm. On the last holiday nobody was in the dorm. Everyone went to their hometowns. I didn't go anywhere. Someday I want to go to my hometown too.

questions.q: Where does the writer live?
What does the writer do every morning?
questions.a: Takes a walk in front of the dorm.

questions.q: Why was nobody in the dorm on the holiday?
